policy: Curated a practical visitor-context subset for food, toilets, viewpoints, parking and ferry/bridge orientation. Records remain current context, not historic date evidence.

curated.summary: Queensferry Museum covers historic Queensferry, Dalmeny, the Forth bridges and local traditions from a High Street visitor stop.
Maid of the Forth is the Hawes Pier boat-trip operator for sightseeing cruises under the bridges and towards Inchcolm.
Forth Bridges Viewpoint is a signed trail stop for broad views of the three Forth crossings and the Firth of Forth.
Forth Railway Bridge Viewpoint is a waterfront stop for close views of the World Heritage rail bridge.
Forth Bridges is a current viewpoint marker for seeing the three crossings together from South Queensferry.
Port Edgar is the marina stop west of the historic core, with bridge views, boat activity, food and marina visitor services.
Hawes is a Forth Bridges Trail stop by Hawes Pier, useful for cruises, bridge views and boat-trip boarding.
The Harbour is a signed trail stop linking the historic High Street, waterfront and bridge-view route.
High Street is the main historic visitor spine, with museum, independent shops, food stops and bridge-trail signs.
The Binks is a signed Forth Bridges Trail stop on the South Queensferry waterfront route.
Public toilets near Queensferry High Street, useful for the historic core, museum and waterfront walk.
Accessible public toilets at the Hawes Pier and bridge-view end of the waterfront.
Public toilets by the Forth Bridges Viewpoint and south-tower trail area, mapped with wheelchair access and daytime hours.
The Little Bakery is a High Street bakery/cafe stop for breakfast, brunch, cakes, coffee and afternoon tea.
Manna House Bakery is a High Street bakery and cafe known for in-house baking and views towards the Three Bridges.
Scotts of Port Edgar is a marina restaurant with bridge views and visitor-friendly food service.
Outboard by Scotts is a Port Edgar cafe beside the marina, useful for casual food during a bridge or harbour visit.
The Railbridge Bistro is a bridge-view waterfront restaurant near Hawes Pier.
The Crab and Lobster Fish Shack is a casual fish-and-chip and seafood stop near the A90/Ferrymuir visitor approach.
curated.sourceOrganisation: The Crab and Lobster Fish Shack

curated.summary: Down the Hatch is a North American-style food stop on Port Edgar Road, better paired with marina or bridge visits than the historic core.
Hawes Pier parking is the most useful mapped parking cluster for bridge views, cruises and the east waterfront.
High Street surface parking supports short visits to Queensferry Museum, cafes and the historic waterfront core.
Forth Bridges Viewpoint parking supports the south-tower viewpoint, bridge-trail signs and public toilets.
Port Edgar parking supports marina visits, boat activity, food stops and bridge views west of the historic core.
Ferry Glen and Back Braes is the key green walking context behind the waterfront, linking village routes with bridge-view approaches.
King George V Park is the main current recreation ground context for South Queensferry.
